> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `os serve (command, 31 pages)`
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0e9a1a4dc68bdf047b53f5940c8df45cacd7c0fc` — the merge of head `66e7f58fd5e181eeffa28a1b9aa8d0d49ef6a176` into base `275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0e9a1a4dc68bdf047b53f5940c8df45cacd7c0fc && git checkout 0e9a1a4dc68bdf047b53f5940c8df45cacd7c0fc
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 66e7f58fd5e181eeffa28a1b9aa8d0d49ef6a176 && git checkout -B drift-repro 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02 && git merge --no-ff 66e7f58fd5e181eeffa28a1b9aa8d0d49ef6a176

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 275ad4229a791f31ec90da4a14621cd54a0dad02` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `66e7f58fd5e181eeffa28a1b9aa8d0d49ef6a176`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #22989, its body and all ten comments (ruling `6125390666`, slice-2 claim `6126676359`, dev report `6129082934`; the seat's ACCEPT `6129114437` read as a claim, never a verdict); PR #23078's body and file list; the net diff against merge-base `0a29bec6a3` (8 files, +753 / -27); the source at the head for every file the census names; the check-runs on the head. Reading time 2026-10-12T17:35Z.

**Check-runs on the head, latest per name:** 31 success, 8 skipped (roster rows: Auto Label, Build Docs, Check PR Size, Console Pin Gate, the dogfood shard matrix, Dogfood Verify CLI, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance), 1 queued at reading time: the aggregate `Test Core` job, whose six shards (1/6 through 6/6) had each concluded success at the same reading. Nothing concluded red. Judged on what concluded; the governed-surface, Part-of, card-claim and single-writer guards all concluded success.

### ① Derived judgments

**A, the composition in `packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts`.** `hostConfigMetadataDoor` is constructed under exactly three conditions, `!devArtifactDoor`, `isHostConfig(config)`, and no plugin in `plugins` named `com.objectstack.metadata` or constructed as `MetadataPlugin`, and `kernel.use`d once, after `serverPlugin`, at the dev door's site. Read against the boot-mode dispatch (`useArtifactFallback || shouldBootWithLibrary(config)`), the boots it reaches are: (a) a non-dev `os serve` of a host config; (b) `os start` beside a host config: `start.ts` compiles the config and hands the path on `OS_INTERNAL_ARTIFACT_PATH`, and in the child `cwdConfigJoinsBoot` / `isConfigCompiledArtifact` answers true for the config's own `dist/objectstack.json`, so the host module loads and this branch runs, supported by source, HTTP NOT MEASURED; (c) and (d) `os serve --dev` of a host config with no artifact on disk, since the dev door composes only when its bytes exist; (e) `--no-server`, since `flags.server` false keeps the dev door out and the door then mounts no routes for want of an HTTP server. Not reached: the dev artifact door's boots (`!devArtifactDoor`); every library boot and the artifact fallback, because `createStandaloneStack` and `createDefaultHostConfig` put a `com.objectstack.metadata` plugin into the merged `plugins` and the third condition refuses; `OS_MODE=off` and `bootMode: 'off'` bare configs, because `isHostConfig` is false. RIGHT: every reached boot is an `os serve` host-config boot whose composition holds no `MetadataPlugin`, the ruling's A verbatim, and no boot the ruling names is missed. The `os start` item is a measurement gap, not a reach gap: the child executes this same file, under the production posture the census measured by hand on the showcase. Recommended, not owed here: one HTTP reading of `os start` beside a host config in a later slice.

**The slot's new occupant on a host-config production boot, against the ten census answers**, each read against the source it names:
1. Loader: `bootstrap: 'lazy'` skips `_loadFromFileSystem`; `eager` with no `artifactSource` scans `rootDir/TYPE/` (`plugin.ts` `start`). Pinned with an `eager` CONTROL that primes an item `lazy` does not. RIGHT.
2. Repository: `FileSystemRepository` attaches under `rootDir/.objectstack/metadata` with `disableWatch` in every mode but `artifact-only`, inside a try/catch; `rootDir` defaults to `process.cwd()` when omitted, so `hostRoot` is load-bearing. Pinned (`rootDir: hostRoot,`; no `.objectstack/metadata` written). RIGHT.
3. Persistence: `MetadataPlugin.init` registers `com.objectstack.metadata-objects` through the manifest service; `metadata-protocol`'s assembly already registers the same four objects on `environmentId === undefined` boots and calls the second registration idempotent and harmless in its own comment. `setDatabaseDriver` / `setDataEngine`: zero non-test callers at the head. RIGHT; the identical 108-table list is the measurement.
4. `/meta` and `openapi.json`: `/meta` reads the ObjectQL registry, so the fifteen types the service lacks were served on BASE and still are; `openapi.json` and `/meta/api` take the matcher when `matchEndpoint` exists and log `no endpoint matcher is reachable` otherwise (`rest-server.ts`, `domains/meta.ts`). Listing the two declared paths is the fix's intended face. RIGHT.
5. Cluster bridge: lane 1 (`service-cluster/src/metadata-cluster-bridge-plugin.ts`) warns when no `attachClusterPubSub`, debug-skips on an in-process driver, attaches otherwise; the manager publishes `metadata.changed` from `notifyWatchers`, which `register()` calls unless `notify: false` and `registerInMemory()` never calls. The boot-time writes on the showcase are `registerInMemory` (the wrap) and ObjectQL's object bridge with `{ notify: false }`, so zero publishes at boot. RIGHT. One thing the census did not name: that bridge (`bridgeObjectsToMetadataService`) now lands its objects on the manager through `register()` instead of the fallback. No loader save (the filesystem loader's contract is `file:`; the save loop takes `datasource:` with `write` only), no notify; its realtime fan-out is gated on a bridged `realtime` service and was not measured. The same path every library boot takes; a census omission, not a defect.
6. Boot cost: 7 interleaved runs each, no claim beyond "not measurable". RIGHT.
7. Dev routes: `registerMetadataHmrRoutes` returns null unless `NODE_ENV` is exactly `development` (`hmr-routes.ts` `isDevMetadataEndpointEnabled`), so the door mounts the SSE route only there. Pinned in process both ways. RIGHT.
8. Security registrar: the wrap's option is `devArtifactDoor ? 'artifact-door' : {}`; the host door is never keyed (`not.toMatch(/hostConfigMetadataDoor\s*\?/)`); with no `artifactSource` the door loads nothing of the stack, so the wrap stays the one registrar. The integration pin serves the fixture's position and capability exactly once. RIGHT; the ⛔ holds.
9. Order: `init` registers the service in Phase 1; the kernel pre-injects fallbacks only for slots no `init` filled, before Phase 2; `registerDeclaredApiEndpoints` runs in `AppPlugin.start`. RIGHT by construction and by the measured log.
10. Which boots: as judged above. RIGHT, with `os start` unmeasured over HTTP.

Nothing moves that the census did not name, beyond the `register()` path noted under 5.

**`kernel.use(hostConfigMetadataDoor)` with no catch.** RIGHT. `kernel.use` throws only when `pluginLoader.load` refuses the plugin; `init` and `start` failures fail `bootstrap` with or without such a catch, and the dev door's catch covers that same narrow class. A door that is the slot's occupant must not fall back to the matcher-less fallback quietly (route rule 3: prefer failing to falling back). Can it fail a boot that served before? Two shapes. (i) `@objectstack/metadata` unresolvable: it is a hard `dependencies` entry (`workspace:*`) of both `@objectstack/cli` and `@objectstack/runtime`, and every library boot and every `os dev` host boot already import it, so such an install was already broken for the default boot. (ii) A host config whose `plugins[]` provides its own `metadata` service under a plugin neither named `com.objectstack.metadata` nor constructed as `MetadataPlugin`: the door registers first (Phase 1 runs in `use` order and the config's plugins are `use`d later), and the host's provider then throws `Service 'metadata' already registered`. No in-tree provider has that shape (`core/src/metadata-service-contract.ts` names two implementations, both covered by the guard), so this is boundary, not defect; see ③.

**B, `packages/runtime/src/app-plugin.ts` `registerDeclaredApiEndpoints`.** Once: `start()` calls the method once per `AppPlugin` instance, no loop, and the new guard sits before the `registerInMemory` guard, so a fallback slot (which has `registerInMemory` and no `matchEndpoint`) warns and still registers. The remedy text is true: `MetadataManager` is the one in-tree `matchEndpoint`. No second matcher: the diff adds a `typeof` read of `matchEndpoint` and nothing else. `warn` is the AGENTS.md level for a functional absence the next caller sees as a 404, not a durability loss. Compositions that now print it: `@objectstack/verify`'s `bootStack` (`kernel.use(new AppPlugin(appBundle))`, no `MetadataPlugin`; the dogfood harness) when the stack declares `apis`; `OS_MODE=off` and `bootMode: 'off'` bare configs with `apis`; any custom kernel without the plugin. That is the ruling's B by name, `bootStack` being its own example. Reach residual: the method returns before the check for a `packages[]` bundle (a pre-existing early return), so a multi-package stack's body `apis` reach a matcher-less slot silently; noted by the dev, zero in-repo producers. The read site is legal under the startup-registry rule: Phase 2, after fallback injection, the verdict logged and recorded nowhere else.

**The reworded dev-door warning.** On the boot that prints it (`os dev` or `serve --dev` over a named artifact not on disk, host config), the old text "Dev metadata-HMR endpoint not enabled" is now false: the host door composes there and mounts the SSE endpoint under `NODE_ENV=development`. The new text "Dev artifact reload not enabled" is true on every boot that prints it, including an `OS_MODE=off` bare config on `--dev`, which gets no host door and still no reload. The second line (the wrap keeps the collections) stays true. The catch-site warning is unchanged and still accurate. RIGHT.

**The two test files outside the claimed list.**
- `boot-preparation-parity.test.ts`: `isHostConfig` was imported but unused in `serve.ts` code at BASE; this diff uses it, `utils/plugin-detection.ts` is a CLOSURE module, so the pin demands a step or a `SERVE_ONLY` reason. The reason is true: `os migrate` boots through `createStandaloneStack`, whose `MetadataPlugin` is always composed (`schema-migration-plugins.ts` header), so the one-shot boot has no door decision to mirror. This is the pin's own exemption mechanism, with its reason; not loosened.
- `serve-host-config-security-registrar.pin.test.ts`: `count('new MetadataPlugin(')` 1 to 2 is true of the file; the pin now holds each construction once and the single `artifactSource: { mode: 'local-file' ... }` spelling once, and the companion pin holds the host door to no `artifactSource` and no registrar keying. The invariant (one artifact door; the registrar keyed on it alone) is preserved; not loosened. The warning literal follows the reword.

**The changeset, sentence by sentence.** The host-config definition: true (`isHostConfig` is any plugin with `init`). `os serve` and `os start` boot the same way: true by source (`configJoins`), HTTP unmeasured for `os start`. `os dev` matched it: measured. 404 to 401 and the undeclared path still 404: measured and pinned. `/meta` byte-for-byte for 22 types: measured at the pre-merge tree; the final-tree `email_template` delta is `main`'s #22990, correctly excluded. `openapi.json` documents the declared endpoints: measured. No new table and no row at boot: measured. Writes nothing into the project directory and roots at the served app: measured, pinned, and confirmed by source (no `datasource:` loader on this door). Reads none of the stack, primes nothing, one registrar: true and pinned. Dev route unmounted unless development, mounted on `--dev` with no artifact: true and pinned. Cluster invalidation attaches with a remote driver and the warning is gone: measured. Boot cost: measured. "One warning per app that declares `apis`": true for single-package bundles; a `packages[]` bundle is exempt, which the PR body states and the changeset does not. `Clause-②: no` is present in the changeset body and on PR body line 2.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/cli` patch, `@objectstack/runtime` patch, `Clause-②: no`. RIGHT. The diff adds no export, no spec key and no config field, and removes nothing authorable (the 27 removed lines are comments and the reworded literal). The HTTP movement, a declared `apis` endpoint answering on a host-config `os serve` where it answered 404, is the published authoring contract (`apis` is a spec surface) honoured on a door that had not honoured it; route rule 3 names the old answer a defect, not an accept set an author or client relies on. `openapi.json`'s accept set is unchanged: it always documented what is mounted (rule 4), and the mounted set moved by the fix. The new `warn` is a log line, not a surface. The `metadata` slot's occupant moving from `createMemoryMetadata` to `MetadataManager` is two implementations of one contract, and the host-config boot now matches what every library boot already receives. The dev SSE route on `--dev` with no artifact is development posture only and the route every other dev boot mounts. A bug fix in released packages takes `patch`, never `skip-changeset`; `no` carries no arm, as required.

### ③ Boundary flags

Deviations, each judged:
1. Two cli test files outside the surface: both required by existing pins, test-only, this lane. Accepted.
2. Reworded dev-door warning: the old text became false on that boot. Accepted.
3. Integration boots run the tsx source entry under the development posture: `check:cli-test-child-env` holds the built-entry spawner set in a script outside the claim, so the production-only fact (no dev route) is pinned in process and the production 401 is the dev's hand measurement on the showcase. Accepted; the residual is stated below.
4. No dogfood pin: `bootStack` composes no `MetadataPlugin`, so it cannot boot this composition; it is where B now speaks. Accepted.
5. Two merges of `main`; census on the pre-merge tree, the final tree re-probed over HTTP (401, 404, dev route 404, `/meta`, `openapi.json`); the two later `main` commits are disjoint from this diff. Accepted.
6. `open_questions`: none.

Out-of-scope findings:
- Finding 1 (`packages/rest/src/openapi-endpoints.ts` `selectDocumentableEndpoints` logs at `error` "fix the declaration rather than the document" when a stored item fails `ApiEndpointSchema`, a `strictObject`, on a runtime-stamped `_diagnostics` key): NEEDS A CARRIER. It is reproducible (measured on BASE's showcase for both items), its remaining reach is exactly the compositions B now targets (`bootStack` and dogfood, `OS_MODE=off`), and an `error` that names a valid declaration as the thing to fix is a metadata-authoring trap under Prime Directive #10. Escalation: the owning seat files it (`area:api`, `packages/rest`). Not a condition on this PR, whose diff does not touch that path.
- Finding 2 (`packages[]` early return before B's check): zero in-repo pull; the PR body states it. A note suffices; a carrier is optional and could ride on the next card that touches the method.

Flags from this review's own reading, none blocking:
- `packages/services/service-cluster/src/metadata-cluster-bridge-plugin.ts` (not in the claim surface) describes the host-config boot as the "fallback metadata slot" shape and calls lane 1's warn "TRUE and VERBATIM on the host-config boot". After this PR that holds only for compositions outside `os serve` (`bootStack`, `OS_MODE=off`). Documentation drift in an untouched file; owed a docs-only follow-up edit, and this record is its note.
- The guard keys on plugin identity (name or constructor) where the kernel's own vocabulary is `providesServices` (`MetadataPlugin` declares `providesServices = ['metadata']`). A third-party `metadata` provider in a host config's `plugins[]` would now fail the boot at `registerService` where it served before. No in-tree producer, and the dev door used the same identity key at BASE. Suggested for a later slice: `p?.providesServices?.includes('metadata')` as the key.
- No CI pin measures a production-posture host-config boot's 401 over HTTP; the production reading is the dev's hand measurement on the showcase plus the in-process dev-route pin. Acceptable for this slice; a built-entry spawner would need `check:cli-test-child-env`'s roster, outside the claim.
- Census omission, not a defect: ObjectQL's `bridgeObjectsToMetadataService` now writes to the manager through `register()` with `notify: false`; no save, no publish; its realtime fan-out is unmeasured and is the path every library boot already takes.
- The aggregate `Test Core` job was queued at reading time with all six shards already success; judged on what concluded.

Governance: the file list touches no governed surface (`Governed Surface Queue Guard` success); the head repo is the base repo, so this is not a fork PR; the PR is draft with `needs:contract-review`, and the queue waits on every check concluding green.
